Title: Scaffold-based generation with MoLeR
Description: MoLeR, a graph-based variational autoencoder from Microsoft Research and Novartis, builds molecules motif by motif from a starting scaffold and was trained on GuacaMol's about 1.5 million drug-like molecules. Ersilia keeps only the Murcko scaffold of the input, discarding its side chains, and decodes onto it the latent codes of random molecules from Enamine's 254k building-block library; the blocks steer the decoder and are not attached. Up to 100 distinct molecules come back, nearly all containing the scaffold and often adding rings. Acyclic inputs return nothing. Unseeded, so runs differ.
Interpretation: Up to 100 molecules built around the input's scaffold by MoLeR, steered by Enamine building-block latent codes.
